earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only Lewis 2013 'North Edoid relations and roots' (comparative wordlist) and Ethnologue; no descriptive phonology of Igwe.

sources.citation: Rolle, Nicholas. 2026. Tone diachrony beyond tonogenesis: Reconstructing the tone melodies of nouns in Proto-Edoid (Niger-Congo). lingbuzz/009572 v3, forthcoming in Diachronica.
sources.note: Family-wide tone database (40 sources, 21 Edoid languages); footnote: 'The Edoid languages not surveyed in this paper are Ikhin-Arokho [ikh], Enwan [env], Ikpeshi [ikp], Igwe [igw], Sasaru [sxs], Iyayu [iya], Akuku [ayk], and Okpe [okx]' -- confirms no tone-marked Igwe description is available even to a 2026 survey. Nothing on Igwe stress.

sources.citation: Schaefer, Ronald P. & Francis O. Egbokhare. 2021. Edo North: Refugium and micro-accretion zone. Abstract, SLE 2021.
sources.note: Regional generalisation only: 'Tone systems contrast high vs. low, with downstep addition in more southerly areas and mid tone west of center.' Igwe not named; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020 [ed. IV]. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation.
sources.note: Entry 409 Sasaru-Enwan-Igwe: Edo State, Akoko-Edo LGA; 3,775 (1952); Benue-Congo: Edoid: North-Central Edoid ii; dialects Enwan, Igwe, Sasaru; 'Refs. Comparative: Elugbe (1989)' only -- no phonology or grammar reference exists for the cluster.

sources.citation: Ethnologue 19 (Lewis, Simons & Fennig 2016), 'Igwe' [igw] public page (Wayback Machine copy)
sources.note: 'Population 47,800 (2000). Location Edo state: Akoko-Edo LGA. Language Status 6a (Vigorous). Classification... Edoid, North-Central, Ghotuo-Uneme-Yekhee.' No alternate names, dialects or language resources listed; nothing on phonology.

sources.citation: Lewis, Demola. 2015. Deciphering Aborigines and Migrants from Cognation and Topography in North-Western Edo. Lengua y Migracion 7(1): 29-51.
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Lexicostatistics only: Table 2b 'Igwe Cognation across Owan' (62-63% with Eese and Ihievbe, 43-52% with the rest); Table 5 'Cognation Percentages for Igwe Sale-Sasaru-Enwa' (Enwa-Igwe c. 50%); 'the Igwe are returnee immigrants' from Akoko-Edo into north-western Owan; fn.2: 'Igwe, Uokha Arokho and Ake all belong to the same migrant party comprising a language cluster. However, Igwe aligns with Ghotou in certain lexical items due to contact.'

sources.citation: Egbokhare, Francis O. 2011. The Sound of Meaning. Inaugural lecture, University of Ibadan.
sources.note: Igwe appears only in Oyakhire's (1997) Owan mutual-intelligibility groups, 'E: Igwe, Ikao, Otuo' (p.69), and in the list of villages where Northern-Edo project audio tapes were recorded. Table 8 'Linguistic Features of NCE and NWE' (tone systems 2 / 2+DS / 3) has no Igwe row. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Elugbe, Ben Ohi. 1989. Edoid. In John Bendor-Samuel (ed.), The Niger-Congo Languages, 291-304. Lanham: University Press of America. (Zenodo 5618102)
sources.note: Igwe appears only as item 'h) Igwe' in the NCE classification list (pp.296-297). Sec. 13.3.4 'Tone systems' (pp.298-299) surveys Degema, Egene, Eruwa, Isoko, Edo, Ghotuo, Oloma, Ibilo, Emhalhe -- no Igwe, no stress statement.

sources.citation: Elugbe, Ben Ohiomamhe. 1989. Comparative Edoid: Phonology and Lexicon (Delta Series 6). Port Harcourt: University of Port Harcourt Press. xvii+253 pp. (Zenodo 5688969, CC-BY)
sources.note: Nothing for Igwe. Igwe is named only on pp.10-11 ('Igwe and Ihievbe (Sebe) of Owan' among clans 'most likely North-Central Edoid peoples') and in the classification list p.24 '(h) Igwe-Enwa-Sasaru', with the footnote that g-i 'are left out of the family tree because their exact relationship with the rest of NCE has not been determined'. No Igwe sketch, no Igwe forms in the lexicon (Glottolog langnote: 'Mentions... Igwe [igw]... but without data'). The word 'stress' does not occur in the text layer.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid igwe1238 (JSON), Wikidata Q3913985, en.wikipedia 'Igwe language' and 'Edoid languages', ISO 639-3 igw record, Joshua Project igw, local Glottolog hh.bib
sources.note: Bibliographic only. Glottolog MED = Lewis 2013 'wordlist_or_less'; hh.bib carries [igw] only in the Elugbe 1989 langnote ('without data') and the Lewis 2013 lgcode ('Igwe-Sale = Igwe [igw], Igwe Oke = Igwe [igw]'). Wikipedia 'Edoid languages' reproduces 12 tone-marked wordlist items each for 'Igwe (Sale)' and 'Igwe (Oke)' attributed to Lewis (2013), showing that the thesis holds tone-marked Igwe wordlists; no prose on tone or stress.

sources.citation: Schaefer, Ronald P. & Francis O. Egbokhare. [2025]. Edoid: Tone in Affirmative and Negative Declarative Clauses. In The Handbook of Multilingualism, Identity, and Language Endangerment in Africa (Springer Handbooks in Languages and Linguistics), ch. 23.
